stream-processing.context: A gear above a flowing wave that ends in an arrow, showing data being processed continuously as it streams past. Used for real time pipelines, event streaming platforms and live data processing settings.

data-connector.context: A database cylinder with a cable leading to a two pin plug. Used for data integrations, connecting a source to a dashboard, and connector libraries in analytics and ETL tools.

linear-gauge.context: A horizontal scale with tick marks and a triangular pointer resting above one position. Used in dashboards for a single value against a range, level indicators and bullet style gauges.

progress-ring.context: A thick ring three quarters complete with a percent sign in its centre. Used for completion percentages, goal progress, loading states and radial progress widgets in dashboards and apps.

survival-curve.context: A descending staircase line on a corner axis with small tick marks on some steps for censored cases. Used for Kaplan Meier survival analysis, customer retention and time to event statistics.

pert-chart.context: Four circles for events joined by arrows that split into two paths and meet again at a final circle. Used for PERT and activity network diagrams, critical path planning and project dependencies.

galton-board.context: A triangle of pegs above a row of bins that hold balls, with the most balls in the middle bin. Used to explain the normal distribution, probability, randomness and the central limit theorem.

active-users.context: Two person busts above a heartbeat style pulse line, standing for people using a product right now. Used for active user counts, live visitors, DAU and MAU metrics and audience dashboards.

device-breakdown.context: A desktop monitor and a phone, each above a small bar of a different height. Used in web and app analytics for traffic split by device type, desktop versus mobile share and platform reports.

attribution-model.context: Three touchpoint dots on the left with lines of different weight converging on a target. Used for marketing attribution, multi touch credit, channel contribution and conversion path analysis.

share-of-voice.context: A megaphone with a small pie chart in front of its mouth. Used for share of voice reports that compare how much a brand is mentioned or advertised against competitors in media and social channels.

gaze-plot.context: A web page with a path of fixation circles of different sizes joined by lines. Used in eye tracking and usability research to show where and in what order people looked at a page.

query-builder.context: A database cylinder beside three stacked condition blocks joined by a bracket. Used for visual query builders, filter rule editors and no code tools that build SQL conditions.

segmented-bar.context: A single long rounded bar divided into four segments of different widths. Used for stacked proportion bars, storage or budget breakdowns and part to whole comparisons in one line.

market-depth-chart.context: Two stepped areas meeting in the middle, the bid side rising to the left and the ask side rising to the right. Used on trading platforms to show order book depth and liquidity around the price.

upset-plot.context: Vertical bars above a matrix of dots where filled dots joined by lines show which sets each bar counts. Used as a clearer alternative to Venn diagrams for many overlapping sets in data science and biology.

significance-bars.context: Two bars of different height joined above by a bracket with an asterisk on top. Used in scientific charts to mark a statistically significant difference between two groups.

data-bottleneck.context: A wide pipe narrowing into a thin neck with dots crowding at the narrow point and one dot passing through. Used for throughput limits, pipeline congestion and performance constraints.

chart-connected-scatter.context: Dots on a corner axis joined in time order by a line that crosses back over itself. Used for connected scatter plots that show how two measures move together over time.

chart-scatter-3d.context: Three axes meeting at a corner with dots floating in the space between them. Used for three dimensional scatter plots, point clouds and multivariate data exploration.

chart-win-loss.context: A row of equal bars along a centre line, some pointing up and some pointing down. Used for win loss sparklines, pass fail streaks and any yes or no result over time.

warming-stripes.context: A square filled with vertical stripes that get wider and denser toward the right, like the climate stripes graphic. Used for temperature change over years, global warming and climate data stories.

flatten-the-curve.context: A tall narrow peak and a low wide curve under a dashed capacity line. Used in public health and epidemiology to show spreading cases over time so they stay below healthcare capacity.

cell-note.context: A spreadsheet grid with a small solid triangle in the top corner of one cell. Used for cell notes and comments, annotation indicators and review markers in spreadsheets.

banded-rows.context: A table with every other row shaded solid. Used for banded or zebra striped table styles that make rows easier to follow in spreadsheets, reports and data grids.

table-totals.context: A table with a heavy rule above the bottom row and a sigma sign in that row. Used for totals rows, sums and summary rows in spreadsheets, reports and data tables.

geo-heatmap.context: A folded map with a blotch of concentric rings over one region. Used for geographic heat maps, density maps, location hotspots and where users or events cluster.

gis-layers.context: Three stacked map planes with a location dot and a road on the top one. Used for GIS software, map layers, overlays and switching spatial data layers on and off.

floor-heatmap.context: A floor plan of rooms with heat blotches where people gather. Used for indoor analytics, occupancy sensors, workplace space utilisation and retail store traffic maps.

foot-traffic.context: Two shoe prints walking beside two bars of a count. Used for footfall and visitor counting, store visits, people counters and retail foot traffic reports.

spike-map.context: A flat map with narrow spikes of different heights rising from several points. Used for spike maps that show values by location, such as population or cases per city.

principal-components.context: A scatter of dots crossed by a long axis arrow and a shorter arrow at right angles to it. Used for principal component analysis, dimensionality reduction and explaining variance in data science.

rage-click.context: A cursor arrow with jagged burst lines around its tip from repeated angry clicks. Used in session replay and UX analytics for rage clicks, user frustration and broken buttons.

form-analytics.context: A form with three input fields, each followed by a bar of different length. Used for form analytics, field completion rates, drop off by field and checkout form optimisation.

email-analytics.context: An envelope with a small bar chart rising out of the top. Used for email campaign reports, open and click rates, newsletter statistics and email marketing dashboards.

video-analytics.context: A video frame with a play button and a declining line along the bottom. Used for video analytics, audience retention, watch time and viewer drop off reports.

social-analytics.context: A speech bubble containing three rising bars. Used for social media analytics, engagement metrics, mentions and community growth reports.

bipartite-graph.context: Two columns of nodes with crossing lines linking nodes on the left to nodes on the right. Used for bipartite graphs, matching problems, two mode networks and recommendation links.

data-feedback-loop.context: Two curved arrows forming a loop around a small bar chart. Used for feedback loops, measure and improve cycles, continuous optimisation and learning from data.

data-anonymization.context: A table whose identifying column is blacked out cell by cell while the other column stays readable. Used for anonymisation, data masking, redaction and privacy protection of personal data.

geocoding.context: An address card with text lines, an arrow and a map pin. Used for geocoding, turning street addresses into map coordinates, address lookup and location search.

decimal-places.context: A decimal point followed by two zeros with an arrow beneath. Used in spreadsheets and number formatting to add decimal places or change the precision of displayed numbers.

text-to-columns.context: A long line of text above an arrow pointing down into a row of three cells. Used for splitting text by a delimiter into separate columns in spreadsheets and data cleaning tools.

deduplicate.context: Two identical table rows joined by a bracket that leads into a single row. Used for removing duplicates, deduplicating records and merging repeated entries in data cleaning.

uniform-distribution.context: A flat topped rectangular shape with straight sides standing on a corner axis. Used for the uniform distribution in probability and statistics, where every value in a range is equally likely.

logarithmic-scale.context: A vertical axis with tick marks that bunch toward the top of each decade and a rising curve beside it. Used for log scales, log axes and data that spans several orders of magnitude.

cloud-analytics.context: A cloud outline with three rising bars inside. Used for cloud based analytics, hosted dashboards, SaaS reporting and data services that run in the cloud.

random-walk.context: A jagged path of short straight steps wandering from a start dot to an end dot. Used for random walks, Brownian motion, stochastic processes and Monte Carlo simulations.

data-mart.context: A small shop front with a striped awning and a database cylinder in the window. Used for data marts, subject focused data stores and departmental slices of a data warehouse.

leaderboard.context: A crown above three ranked rows that get shorter down the list. Used for leaderboards, top performers, high score tables, sales rankings and standings.

comparison-table.context: A table with a label column and two value columns of check marks and crosses. Used for feature comparisons, pricing plan tables and side by side product comparisons.

gap-analysis.context: A short bar and a tall bar with a double arrow measuring the gap between their tops. Used for gap analysis, actual versus target, shortfalls and performance differences.

value-stream-map.context: Two process boxes joined by an arrow above a stepped timeline line. Used for value stream mapping, lean manufacturing, lead time and process waste analysis.

one-to-many-relation.context: A relationship line with a single bar at one end and a three pronged crow's foot at the other. Used in entity relationship diagrams and database design for one to many relationships.

color-scale.context: A legend bar divided into bands from empty to solid with tick marks below. Used for colour scales, heat map keys, gradient legends and value ranges in charts and maps.

crosstab.context: A table whose header row and column are shaded, with the corner cell split by a diagonal. Used for cross tabulations, contingency tables, pivot tables and two way summaries.

regression-residuals.context: Dots above and below a straight fitted line, each joined to it by a short vertical stroke. Used for regression residuals, least squares fitting, prediction error and model diagnostics.

data-journalism.context: A newspaper page with a masthead, lines of text and a small bar chart in one column. Used for data journalism, news graphics, data stories and reporting based on statistics.

swingometer.context: A semicircular dial split into two halves with the needle swung toward one side. Used in election coverage for the swing between two parties and for any two way balance of opinion.

lorenz-curve.context: A corner axis with a straight diagonal and a curve sagging below it. Used for Lorenz curves, the Gini coefficient and measuring inequality of income or wealth.

qq-plot.context: Dots lined up along a diagonal reference line that curl away from it at both ends. Used for quantile quantile plots that check whether data follows a normal or other distribution.

raincloud-plot.context: A half violin shape above a small box plot with a row of scattered dots below it like rain. Used for raincloud plots that show the shape, summary and raw points of a distribution together.

cell-range.context: A spreadsheet grid with a block of cells selected inside a heavy border. Used for cell ranges, selections, named ranges and selecting multiple cells in spreadsheets.

table-autofilter.context: A table whose header cells each hold a small dropdown triangle. Used for autofilter, column filters and sort and filter menus in spreadsheets and data grids.

group-rows.context: Table rows with a bracket joining three of them and a small minus box at the bracket end. Used for grouping and outlining rows, collapsing and expanding sections in spreadsheets.

circular-reference.context: Three cells in a triangle linked by arrows that loop back to the first cell. Used for circular reference warnings, formula loops and circular dependencies in spreadsheets and data models.

trace-precedents.context: Two cells each sending an arrow from a dot into one target cell. Used for formula auditing, trace precedents and trace dependents, and showing which cells feed a calculation.

data-slicer.context: A header bar above a column of pill shaped buttons, with the top and bottom buttons selected. Used for slicers, dashboard filter buttons and quick segment pickers in pivot tables and BI tools.

data-source.context: A database cylinder with three short arrows pointing out of its right side. Used for data sources, feeds, exporting data and the origin of data in pipelines and reports.

data-transformation.context: A square and a circle joined by an arrow above a gear, showing data changing shape through a process. Used for data transformation, ETL steps, mapping and conversion tools.

weighted-graph.context: Three nodes joined by edges of different thickness that stand for their weights. Used for weighted graphs, network costs, shortest path problems and relationship strength.

pie-chart-map.context: A folded map with two small pie charts placed over different regions. Used for maps that show proportions by region, such as vote share or sales mix in each area.

conversion-rate.context: A funnel with a percent sign beneath its narrow spout. Used for conversion rate metrics, funnel conversion, sales pipelines and conversion rate optimisation.

tracking-pixel.context: An envelope with a tiny solid square at its corner sending out signal arcs. Used for tracking pixels, email open tracking, web beacons and privacy warnings about hidden trackers.
